citations.title: The Press Files: Hamas and PIJ military operatives posed as journalists
citations.excerpt: EXPOSED: HAMAS AND PIJ MILITARY OPERATIVES POSED AS JOURNALISTS. THE 170 MILITARY OPERATIVES. Over the past three years of the war, numerous articles, opinion pieces and reports have repeated the claim that the IDF deliberately targets journalists in Gaza, in violation of international law. But that claim does not tell the full story. Individuals presented as innocent journalists were, in fact, militants in the military wings of Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ) and other terrorist organizations. They presented themselves as legitimate media professionals while serving terrorist organizations that regularly use propaganda and psychological warfare. Journalists are expected to report the unbiased truth. Yet these individuals concealed a fundamental truth about themselves: their own roles within miltary wings of terrorist organizations. This page presents an in-depth investigation based on a wide range of intelligence sources, including open-source information, documents gathered in the field, interrogations of military operatives by Israeli intelligence bodies and more. The evidence below exposes what they left out of the story.

citations.title: IDF documents terror affiliations of 170 Palestinian journalists killed in Gaza war
citations.excerpt: IDF documents terror affiliations of 170 Palestinian journalists killed in Gaza war. The Israel Defense Forces on Thursday said it determined that 170 Palestinians in the Gaza Strip who were identified as journalists following their deaths were actually members of terror groups. Following extensive research, the IDF is now revealing that 170 Gazans killed during the war who were presented as journalists and media personnel were in fact serving as terrorists for terror organizations in the Strip, foremost among them Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad, the army said. According to the military, 118 of the journalists were active in Hamas military wing, while 49 operated in Islamic Jihad, two were members of the Popular Resistance Committees, and one was in the Mujahideen Brigades. Seventeen of the people on the list invaded Israeli territory in the October 7, 2023, attack, the army said. Some of the journalists appearing on the IDF list also worked for international media outlets, including Reuters, CNN, BBC, AFP, AP, Le Monde, ABC Australia and others. The 170 names are published by the IDF on a dedicated website. The military said it was publishing verified evidence, including visual material and documents produced by the terror organizations, some of which were found in the field. The IDF said that during the war, various international media outlets repeatedly accused Israel and the IDF, without presenting verified findings, of deliberately harming journalists. This was despite the fact that in some cases the terror organizations themselves presented those individuals as terrorists in their ranks and even claimed responsibility for them, the IDF asserted. The information now being revealed illustrates the gap between the picture presented to the world and the reality on the ground, and presents additional and conclusive evidence that the IDF does not deliberately and systematically target journalists, but rather terror organizations and their terrorists, in accordance with international law, the military added. The Committee to Protect Journalists has removed some names from its list of journalists killed in the war, after they were revealed to be terror operatives.

citations.title: IDF: 170 alleged journalists killed in Gaza were Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad terrorists
citations.excerpt: IDF: 170 alleged journalists killed in Gaza were Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad terrorists. The IDF revealed on Thursday that 170 individuals who were misleadingly presented as civilian journalists killed in strikes on Gaza were actually affiliated with Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ), and other terrorist organizations. The journalists identities and terrorist affiliations were verified using documentation released by the terrorist organizations themselves and materials recovered by Israeli troops during Gaza operations, the military stated. The IDF launched a website dedicated to compiling information regarding terrorists found to be misrepresenting themselves as civilian journalists and combating accusations that the IDF deliberately targets civilians working in the media. Earlier on Thursday, the IDF released a statement highlighting ten journalists who doubled as Hamas and PIJ terrorists. The terrorists, some of whom worked for news outlets such as Reuters, Turkish state-run Anadolu Agency, and Palestine Now News Agency, operated as snipers, commanders, trainers, and propaganda agents, among other roles. According to the IDF, some of the alleged journalists infiltrated Israel and participated in Hamas October 7 massacre. Hamas terrorist Asem Adli Ahmed al-Barsh, an alleged journalist for Palestinian Al-Rai Radio, was named by Reporters Without Borders (RSF) in a December 2023 complaint to the International Criminal Court. RSF accused Israel of deliberately targeting civilian journalists and did not mention Barsh status as a Hamas terrorist in the complaint. A number of the terrorists named by the IDF were included in the Committee to Protect Journalists database of journalists and media workers killed in Gaza since 2023.

citations.title: IDF kills two October 7 terrorists in Gaza strikes, including Beeri hostage abductor
citations.excerpt: IDF kills two October 7 terrorists in Gaza strikes, including Beeri hostage abductor. The Hamas terrorists infiltrated on October 7 and kidnapped Sharon Hertzman-Avigdori, Noam Avigdori, Adi Shoham, Nave Shoham, Yahel Shoham, and Shoshan Haran to the Gaza Strip. The IDF killed Muhammad Jamal Mahmoud Abu Al-Shaar and Musab Abd al-Jalil Saqib Balbisi in a Thursday statement. The IDF killed two terrorists during strikes on Gaza on Tuesday, one of whom abducted seven hostages on October 7th from Kibbutz Beeri. The military announced on Thursday that it killed Muhammad Jamal Mahmoud Abu Al-Shaar in a strike on Gaza City, as well as Palestinian Islamic Jihad terrorist Musab Abd al-Jalil Saqib Balbisi in a strike on Jabalya. Abu Al-Shaar was a cell commander in Hamas military wing, the Izzadin al-Qassam Brigades. He infiltrated Kibbutz Beeri on October 7 and kidnapped Sharon Hertzman-Avigdori, Noam Avigdori, Adi Shoham, Nave Shoham, Yahel Shoham, and Shoshan Haran to the Gaza Strip. All of the aforementioned former hostages were released in November 2023. Balbisi also infiltrated southern Israel during the October 7 massacre, the IDF stated. He was a commander in PIJ military wing. The military said that both of them were responsible for planning terror attacks against Israeli citizens.

citations.title: US sanctions target Iran auto, rail sectors as blockade chokes ship lanes
citations.excerpt: US sanctions target Iran auto, rail sectors as blockade chokes ship lanes. WASHINGTON, Oct 1 (Reuters) - The Trump administration imposed sanctions on Iran rail and auto sectors and their foreign suppliers, the Treasury Department said on Thursday, widening its wartime economic campaign to isolate Tehran. The sanctions are part of the department Operation Economic Outcast, announced August 24, which aims to cut Tehran funding for the war, missile construction, cyberattacks and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps or IRGC. The move extends US economic pressure on Iran from sea to land, targeting sectors Tehran has leaned on since a naval blockade cut off its oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. The US blockade of Iranian ports has forced Tehran to rely more on autos and rail for transporting petroleum, fertilizer, chemicals and other goods. Thursday sanctions target those alternatives, according to the Treasury Department. The sanctions designate Iran Khodro Company, or IKCO, and SAIPA Iranian Automobile Manufacturing Company, or SAIPA. Treasury said the two companies represent more than 90% of Iran domestic auto market. Treasury also designated the state-owned Islamic Republic of Iran Railway Company. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the action directly targets Iran enablers and lays the groundwork for the United States and our partners to drain the regime revenue once and for all. Thursday sanctions also target foreign companies in Indonesia, the UAE and Turkey that supply Iran auto industry.

passages.text: The Israel-local Thursday window was dominated by an information fight, not a new front. The IDF published The Press Files, saying individuals presented as innocent journalists were militants in the military wings of Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad, and that the page holds 170 military operatives.

Alongside the dossier, the army said it killed October 7 infiltrators in Gaza, including Beeri cell commander Muhammad Jamal Mahmoud Abu Al-Shaar. Separately, Reuters reported US sanctions on Iran auto and rail sectors after a naval blockade cut oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.

The Times of Israel quoted the army: 170 Gazans presented as journalists were serving as terrorists, 118 in Hamas military wing, 49 in Islamic Jihad, and 17 who invaded Israeli territory on October 7, 2023. Some names also worked for Reuters, CNN, BBC, AFP, AP, Le Monde and ABC Australia.

The Jerusalem Post reported a Thursday announcement that Abu Al-Shaar was killed in Gaza City and Musab Abd al-Jalil Saqib Balbisi in Jabalya. Abu Al-Shaar kidnapped Sharon Hertzman-Avigdori, Noam Avigdori, Adi Shoham, Nave Shoham, Yahel Shoham and Shoshan Haran from Kibbutz Beeri; those former hostages were released in November 2023.

The IDF Press Files page says the claim that the IDF deliberately targets journalists in Gaza does not tell the full story, and that the evidence exposes what they left out. The Times of Israel quoted the army saying it does not deliberately and systematically target journalists, but rather terror organizations and their terrorists, in accordance with international law.

Reuters reported that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the Thursday action directly targets Iran enablers and lays the groundwork for the United States and our partners to drain the regime revenue once and for all. The designations also cover foreign suppliers in Indonesia, the UAE and Turkey.

Watch whether Reuters, the BBC, AFP, AP and the Committee to Protect Journalists respond entry by entry to the 170 names, and whether the Committee to Protect Journalists removes further names after they were revealed to be terror operatives. Independent review of each file is not in this packet.
